You find the officially stated REASON for one amendment to an Indian statute, in
the evidence passages given (and only there).
A reason says WHY (purpose, objective, problem addressed: "in order to", "with a view to",
"to ensure", "it has been decided", "difficulties were noticed ..."). A sentence that only
says WHAT the amendment does is not a reason.
If a passage states a reason for THIS amendment, copy it exactly: one to three contiguous
sentences, word for word, at most 80 words. If no passage does, answer found=false.
Reply in JSON only:
{"found": true|false, "passage": "<passage id>", "quote": "<verbatim text>",
 "claim": "<one sentence giving the stated reason, adding nothing the quote does not say>"}

Amendment: section 11 of Act 3/2016, amending s23 of the principal Act (Statements of claim and defence.)
Instruction (start): In section 23 of the principal Act, after sub-section (2), the following sub-section shall be inserted, namely:— “(2A) The respondent, in support of his case, may also submit a counterclaim or plead a set-off, which shall be adjudicated upon by the arbitral tribunal, if such counterclaim or set-off falls within the scope of the arbitration agreement.”.

It is further noticed that the whole of Section 17 of the principal Act has been substituted by a new Section. The new provisions of Section 17
empower the arbitral tribunal with power and discretion to grant extensive interim relief.
It is noticed again that provisions of Section 23, 24 and 25 have also been amended and new Sections 25A, 29A and 29B have been inserted
by the amending Bill. By these provisions, the Arbitral Award is to be made within a period of 12 months; and if the parties agree, they may fast-track the procedure to conclude the arbitration in six months. Section 31 has also been amended. A new Section 31A has been incorporated by this
amending Bill.
